post.name: flux-identity
post.content:
#!/bin/sh
# FluxBilling: identity from kernel cmdline (fluxhost= fluxpass=).
# Runs in the live env after install; target is mounted at /mnt.
# root ships LOCKED in the profile above - this profile is readable in the
# live environment and is archived with the install logs, so it must never
# carry a usable password. No fallback either: a missing fluxpass= leaves the
# accounts locked rather than handing out a default published in a public repo.
C=$(cat /proc/cmdline)
zget() { echo "$C" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p" | head -n1; }
H=$(zget fluxhost); [ -n "$H" ] || H=fluxserver
P=$(zget fluxpass)
echo "$H" > /mnt/etc/hostname
chroot /mnt /bin/sh -c "id user >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -c 'Default User' user"
if [ -n "$P" ]; then
  # stdin, never argv or a nested sh -c: the password must not appear on any
  # command line or be re-parsed by a shell - metacharacters in it would
  # break the command or execute inside the target chroot.
  printf 'root:%s\nuser:%s\n' "$P" "$P" | chroot /mnt chpasswd
else
  echo "FLUX: no fluxpass= on the kernel command line - root and user stay LOCKED." >&2
fi
unset P
sed -i 's/^#\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /mnt/etc/ssh/sshd_config
chroot /mnt systemctl enable sshd
# The kernel command line reaches the installation logs - and on this family
# it carries the password TWICE: fluxpass= and live.password=. Worse, Agama
# copies its logs onto the target AFTER post scripts run (CopyLogsStep follows
# PostScripts in the storage finisher), so an inline scrub can never reach
# them. Redact what is already there, then install a first-boot oneshot for
# whatever Agama copies later. The oneshot deletes compressed archives under
# the install-log dirs outright: Agama bundles the live journal (cmdline
# included) as a tarball sed cannot reach inside.
find /mnt/var/log -type f 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
  sed -i -e 's/fluxpass=[^[:space:]]*/fluxpass=<redacted>/g' \
         -e 's/live\.password=[^[:space:]]*/live.password=<redacted>/g' "$f" 2>/dev/null || :
done
cat > /mnt/usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub <<'FLUXEOF'
#!/bin/sh
for d in /var/log/agama-installation /var/log/YaST2; do
    [ -d "$d" ] || continue
    find "$d" -type f \( -name '*.gz' -o -name '*.xz' -o -name '*.zst' -o -name '*.bz2' -o -name '*.tar*' \) -exec rm -f {} + 2>/dev/null || :
    find "$d" -type f 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
        sed -i -e 's/fluxpass=[^[:space:]]*/fluxpass=<redacted>/g' \
               -e 's/live\.password=[^[:space:]]*/live.password=<redacted>/g' "$f" 2>/dev/null || :
    done
done
systemctl disable flux-scrub.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/flux-scrub.service /usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub
FLUXEOF
chmod 700 /mnt/usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub
cat > /mnt/etc/systemd/system/flux-scrub.service <<'FLUXEOF'
[Unit]
Description=FluxBilling: strip install-time credentials from installer logs
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/flux-scrub

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
FLUXEOF
chroot /mnt systemctl enable flux-scrub.service
